stem: A Massachusetts-licensed health care facility has no on-site pharmacy. Its outside pharmacy provider wants to place an automated dispensing device (ADD) in a patient-care area. Before the ADD is used, what is the best compliance step?
choices: Use it once the pharmacy owns every medication loaded into the cabinet.
Ownership does not replace facility approval.
Obtain approval for the ADD's use and placement from the facility's licensing body.
Policy requires licensing-body approval.
Obtain only a new wholesaler permit for the outside pharmacy.
A wholesaler permit is not the stated approval.
Begin use after the pharmacy's manager of record signs an internal memo.
Internal approval alone is insufficient.
Delay approval until the first Schedule II medication is stocked.
Approval is not triggered only by C-II stock.
steps: Identify that the facility lacks an on-site pharmacy
Apply the ADD facility-approval condition
core: A facility without an on-site pharmacy needs licensing-body approval for ADD use and placement.
facts: The ADD policy applies to Massachusetts-licensed health care facilities.
trap: Confusing pharmacy ownership of stock with facility authorization.
distinct: New facility-authorization fork; not generic controlled-stock security.
anti_guess: Every option names a plausible approval or timing event.

stem: A hospital unit receives a pharmacy-supplied ADD containing several patient-care medications. A nurse asks whether the facility owns the medications once they are loaded into the cabinet. Under the Massachusetts ADD policy, which answer is most accurate?
choices: The facility owns them immediately when the ADD door is closed.
Loading does not transfer ownership.
The nurse owns custody of them after the first cabinet login.
Access is not ownership.
The pharmacy retains ownership until the medication is dispensed for administration.
That is the policy's ownership point.
The patient owns every dose as soon as an order is entered.
An order alone does not transfer ADD ownership.
Ownership transfers to the wholesaler whenever a dose is returned.
The wholesaler is not the default owner.
steps: Identify ADD stock before dispensing
Locate the policy's ownership-transfer point
core: Medication in the ADD remains pharmacy property until dispensed for administration.
facts: Facility access and pharmacy ownership are separate concepts.
trap: Treating physical custody as legal ownership.
distinct: No existing item tests ownership of ADD contents.
anti_guess: All choices use realistic custody milestones.

stem: A patient is admitted to a Massachusetts facility with an ADD. The cabinet contains the requested medication, but no valid patient-specific prescription or medication order has yet been entered. What should occur?
choices: Remove a dose because presence in the ADD itself authorizes administration.
Stocking is not dispensing authority.
Use the dose if a technician verbally confirms the usual regimen.
Technician confirmation is not a valid order.
Wait for a valid patient-specific prescription or order before dispensing the medication from the ADD.
A valid patient-specific order is required.
Treat every ADD item as floor stock that needs no patient-specific authorization.
The policy does not create blanket floor-stock authority.
Dispense now and obtain the order only if a controlled substance was selected.
The order condition is not limited to federal controls.
steps: Separate cabinet inventory from dispensing authority
Require the patient-specific prescription or order
core: ADD availability does not substitute for a valid patient-specific prescription or order.
facts: The device stores medication; it does not create prescriptive authority.
trap: Assuming stocked medication is automatically authorized for a patient.
distinct: Different from Q0118 prescription elements; this is the ADD access prerequisite.
anti_guess: Distractors reflect real floor-stock and verbal-order confusions.

stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy audits its ADD program. Which records or data should be retained as part of the ADD record system? Select all that apply.
choices: Documentation of required approval for the ADD location
Approval documentation belongs in the record set.
ADD transaction data showing product, patient identifier, date/time, and reconciliation
Transaction and reconciliation data are required.
Records of ADD maintenance and personnel access/events
Maintenance and access events are tracked.
Only the final monthly narcotic purchase invoice, with all ADD transaction data discarded
Invoices alone do not replace ADD event records.
A verbal recollection from the charge nurse instead of a retrievable transaction record
Verbal recollection is not the required record.
steps: Identify ADD-specific record categories
Reject substitutes that omit device-event accountability
core: ADD records include approvals, device/event information, access, transaction details, and reconciliation rather than a single purchase record.
facts: The pharmacy maintains ADD records for at least two years under the policy.
trap: Substituting ordinary purchasing records for ADD accountability records.
distinct: Distinct from DEA two-year controlled-substance retention; this tests ADD event content.
anti_guess: Three operational records compete with two plausible but incomplete substitutes.

stem: A pharmacy is preparing medications for an ADD at a Massachusetts health care facility. Which actions are consistent with the current ADD policy? Select all that apply.
choices: Load a manufacturer's sealed original single-dose package when suitable
Sealed original packaging is acceptable.
Use medication repackaged according to professional standards for a single dose or person
Proper single-dose/person repackaging is permitted.
Report medication losses according to the pharmacy licensing body's requirements
Loss reporting follows licensing-body requirements.
Pour several loose tablets from different lots into one unlabeled common cup to simplify restocking
That defeats package integrity and accountability.
Ignore a documented shortage if all missing doses are Schedule VI
Schedule VI status does not erase accountability.
steps: Classify acceptable ADD package presentation
Apply loss-accountability requirements
core: ADD stock must preserve appropriate package integrity and medication losses remain reportable under applicable licensing requirements.
facts: Single-dose/person packaging supports traceability.
trap: Assuming lower schedules eliminate device accountability.
distinct: New ADD package/loss fork, not the federal significant-loss reporting question.
anti_guess: Incorrect options are operational shortcuts a real site might consider.

stem: A retail pharmacy uses an approved ADD as an emergency medication kit. Which personnel/loading statements are consistent with Massachusetts policy? Select all that apply.
choices: A pharmacy technician may load Schedule III through VI medications
Ordinary technician authority is limited to III-VI here.
A certified pharmacy technician may load the emergency-kit ADD
Certified technicians are listed loaders.
A pharmacy intern may load the emergency-kit ADD
Interns are listed loaders.
An ordinary pharmacy technician may load Schedule II simply because the device is an emergency kit
The ordinary-tech boundary excludes C-II.
Only a pharmacist may ever load the emergency-kit ADD
Policy lists additional authorized personnel.
steps: Identify retail emergency-kit ADD use
Match each credential to the loading rule
core: Emergency-kit ADD loading permits several credentials, but an ordinary technician is limited to Schedules III-VI.
facts: A licensed nurse is also an authorized loader under the policy.
trap: Applying the certified-technician privilege to an ordinary technician.
distinct: Special ADD loading privilege differs from Q0075 generic technician scope.
anti_guess: Each option pairs a real credential with a real schedule issue.

stem: A retail pharmacy plans to use an ADD for routine medication dispensing rather than only as an emergency kit. Which controls apply? Select all that apply.
choices: Obtain a machine-specific DEA registration and Controlled Substance Registration as required by the policy
Routine retail ADD use carries machine-specific registrations.
Continuously monitor the ADD by video
Continuous video monitoring is required.
Have it loaded by a certified pharmacy technician or pharmacy intern under Massachusetts pharmacist supervision
Those are the listed routine loaders.
Allow any unlicensed cashier to load Schedule VI items if a pharmacist is in the building
Unlicensed cashiers are not authorized loaders.
Treat the machine as exempt from pharmacy policies because it is computer controlled
ADD use remains subject to policies and law.
steps: Distinguish routine retail dispensing from emergency-kit use
Apply machine registration, monitoring, and loader requirements
core: Routine retail ADD dispensing adds machine-specific registration, continuous video, and credentialed supervised loading requirements.
facts: General ADD safety, security, and accountability duties still apply.
trap: Importing the broader emergency-kit loader list into routine dispensing.
distinct: No current question tests machine-specific ADD registration/video controls.
anti_guess: All options describe plausible automation governance choices.

stem: A pharmacy technician trainee is assigned to restock an ADD at a satellite Massachusetts clinic. The clinic is licensed, but it has no on-site pharmacy and the ADD address is different from the pharmacy's MCSR address. Can the trainee use the special 2023 ADD-stocking pathway?
choices: Yes, because trainee status alone authorizes ADD stocking at any licensed clinic.
Facility prerequisites must also be met.
Yes, if only Schedule VI products are involved.
Schedule does not cure the location prerequisites.
No; the special pathway requires a Massachusetts-licensed health care facility with an on-site pharmacy and ADDs at the same physical address listed on the facility MCSR.
Both location prerequisites are missing.
No, because trainees may never perform inventory functions involving an ADD.
Eligible trainees have defined ADD functions.
Yes, after the trainee obtains a personal DEA registration.
A personal DEA registration is not the policy solution.
steps: Identify the special technician-stocking policy
Check on-site pharmacy and MCSR-address prerequisites
core: The PTT ADD pathway is location-limited and cannot be used at the described off-site clinic.
facts: The pharmacy must also maintain policies and training for the permitted activities.
trap: Checking only schedule or credential while ignoring facility prerequisites.
distinct: Q0075 tests generic technician scope, not the ADD policy's location gate.
anti_guess: Several answers would be plausible if only credential or schedule mattered.

stem: At an eligible hospital ADD, a pharmacy technician trainee works under pharmacist direction and supervision but without direct pharmacist supervision. Which tasks may the trainee perform under the Massachusetts ADD stocking policy? Select all that apply.
choices: Transport and load pharmacist-verified Schedule III-VI stock using barcode or other electronic validation
This is an expressly permitted PTT function.
Verify expiration dates and remove expired Schedule III-VI stock using electronic validation
Expired-stock removal is permitted.
Load an unverified Schedule IV bottle based only on the trainee's visual check
PTT loading requires pharmacist-verified stock.
Transport and load Schedule II stock under the PTT pathway
PTT stocking is limited to III-VI.
Override a clinical interaction warning before the dose is released
Clinical judgment is outside this inventory exception.
steps: Identify trainee rather than licensed-technician privileges
Apply verification, schedule, and electronic-validation conditions
core: A PTT may perform defined pharmacist-verified Schedule III-VI inventory functions, not C-II or clinical judgment tasks.
facts: The activity remains under pharmacist direction and supervision.
trap: Equating absence of direct supervision with independent practice.
distinct: This is a narrow inventory/stocking exception, not generic technician judgment.
anti_guess: Wrong choices are adjacent functions that differ by one controlling condition.

stem: A nationally certified Massachusetts-licensed pharmacy technician is using the special ADD stocking pathway without prior pharmacist verification. Which conditions must be satisfied? Select all that apply.
choices: The medication is non-patient-specific Schedule VI stock
The shortcut is limited to nonpatient-specific S-VI.
The medication is not a PMP drug such as gabapentin
PMP drugs are excluded from this shortcut.
Barcode scanning or other electronic validation is used
Electronic validation is part of the pathway.
The technician may open bulk stock and repackage individual doses during the transfer
Further manipulation is not permitted.
The same no-prior-verification shortcut extends to Schedule V because the technician is nationally certified
The pathway is Schedule VI only.
steps: Identify nationally certified licensed technician status
Apply Schedule VI, PMP, packaging, and electronic-validation limits
Reject broader technician privileges
core: The no-prior-verification shortcut is narrowly limited to nonpatient-specific, non-PMP Schedule VI stock transferred without further manipulation using electronic validation.
facts: Manufacturer-sealed original packaging is an example of no further manipulation.
trap: Treating national certification as authority to bypass schedule or PMP limits.
distinct: New credential+schedule+PMP multi-layer pathway.
anti_guess: Every option states a realistic stocking condition; four separate legal facts must be classified.

stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy receives a prescription marked 'EPT' for the untreated sex partner of a patient diagnosed with gonorrhea but not chlamydia. The prescription otherwise appears valid. Under the Board/DCP EPT dispensing policy, what is the key issue?
choices: The EPT pharmacy policy applies to every sexually transmitted infection.
The policy is not universal to all STIs.
The policy's EPT pathway is limited to treatment of chlamydia, so this gonorrhea-only case does not fit it.
Chlamydia is the stated scope.
EPT is allowed only for viral infections.
That is not the policy distinction.
EPT is limited to controlled substances in Schedules II-V.
Scheduling is not the eligibility criterion.
The partner must first become a registered pharmacy technician.
Partner credential is irrelevant.
steps: Identify the diagnosed infection
Apply the chlamydia-only EPT policy scope
core: Massachusetts pharmacy EPT dispensing policy applies only to chlamydia treatment.
facts: EPT treats a partner without examination or testing under this policy.
trap: Assuming one EPT process automatically covers every STI.
distinct: EPT is absent from the current 130-question bank.
anti_guess: Other infectious-condition options are clinically plausible but legally outside this policy.

stem: A prescriber is issuing separate Massachusetts EPT prescriptions for partners of a patient with confirmed chlamydia. Which prescription-identification approaches are acceptable under the EPT policy? Select all that apply.
choices: Issue the partner prescription using the partner's actual name when known
A named-partner prescription is allowed.
Use 'Expedited Partner Therapy' in place of the partner's name and address
The full EPT designation is permitted.
Use 'EPT' in place of the partner's name and address
The abbreviation is expressly permitted.
Put the index patient's name on one prescription and silently dispense extra doses for unnamed partners without separate partner prescriptions
The policy calls for a separate partner prescription.
Leave all patient-identification fields blank with no EPT designation
The EPT designation supplies the permitted replacement.
steps: Confirm chlamydia EPT context
Classify each partner-identification route independently
core: The partner may be named, or an approved EPT designation may replace the partner's name and address on a separate prescription.
facts: E.P.T. is also an accepted designation.
trap: Turning an identity exception into permission for a blank or combined prescription.
distinct: New patient-identity exception; Q0118 tests ordinary prescription elements.
anti_guess: Three correct forms and two realistic shortcuts force independent evaluation.

stem: A valid chlamydia-partner prescription uses 'EPT' instead of a partner name and address. The pharmacist decides to fill it. How should the pharmacy handle the patient profile and prescription label?
choices: Create the profile and label using the EPT designation in place of the partner's name and address.
That is the instructed anonymous EPT workflow.
Use the index patient's profile and label so no new record exists.
The partner prescription gets its own EPT record.
Use the prescriber's name as the patient identifier.
The prescriber does not replace the partner identifier.
Dispense with no patient profile because EPT prescriptions are exempt from pharmacy records.
The policy instructs creation of a profile.
Invent a fictitious first and last name for the partner.
The EPT designation is the permitted identifier.
steps: Recognize an anonymous but valid EPT prescription
Apply the EPT profile and label instruction
core: The pharmacy creates a separate profile and label using an approved EPT designation.
facts: Anonymous EPT does not eliminate the pharmacy record.
trap: Using the index patient's identity for the partner's prescription.
distinct: Downstream documentation fork rather than EPT eligibility.
anti_guess: Every option offers a plausible way to construct an anonymous record.

stem: A pharmacist receives a valid Massachusetts chlamydia EPT prescription but is unable or unwilling to fill it. What does the Board/DCP policy direct the pharmacist to do?
choices: Destroy the prescription so it cannot be filled elsewhere.
The policy does not authorize destruction.
Refer the patient to an alternate pharmacy.
Referral is the specified action.
Tell the patient that no Massachusetts pharmacy may fill EPT.
That misstates the policy.
Convert the prescription to an ordinary OTC sale.
EPT status does not create OTC status.
Hold it indefinitely until the original patient returns with the partner.
That defeats the referral requirement.
steps: Confirm the prescription fits EPT policy
Apply the unable/unwilling-to-fill referral duty
core: A pharmacist who cannot or will not fill a valid EPT prescription must refer to an alternate pharmacy.
facts: The policy gives a specific continuity action rather than a dispensing mandate.
trap: Confusing permission not to fill with permission to block access.
distinct: New mandatory EPT referral action.
anti_guess: Distractors are realistic disposition choices for an unfilled prescription.

stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is reviewing requests to administer prescribed medications. Which requests fall within current Massachusetts pharmacist-administration categories, assuming all training, prescription, and guidance conditions are satisfied? Select all that apply.
choices: A listed long-acting injectable antipsychotic for treatment of mental illness under prescriber direction
Mental-illness administration is an authorized category subject to guidance.
Extended-release naltrexone for substance use disorder under the applicable guidance
SUD administration is an authorized category.
Prescribed testosterone for gender-affirming care
Current statute expressly includes this category.
Any prescription-only drug for any diagnosis merely because the patient prefers pharmacy administration
Authority is not an unlimited administration license.
A routine maintenance injection for an unrelated indication solely because the product is Massachusetts Schedule VI
Schedule VI status alone does not create administration authority.
steps: Identify each drug/indication pair
Match it to a current pharmacist-administration category
Reject schedule-only reasoning
core: Massachusetts pharmacist administration is category- and condition-specific, including covered MH/SUD therapy and prescribed testosterone for gender-affirming care.
facts: Current law also includes certain STI/HIV-related administration categories.
trap: Turning enumerated administration authority into authority for any injectable prescription.
distinct: New scope domain, separate from contraception prescribing and naloxone access.
anti_guess: Authorized and unauthorized options are all plausible pharmacy-administered therapies.

stem: A trained Massachusetts pharmacist has Vivitrol in stock and a patient asks for an injection today. There is no patient-specific prescription or prescriber direction for this dose. What is the best action under the MH/SUD administration guidance?
choices: Administer because Vivitrol appears on the eligible-medication list.
Drug eligibility does not replace patient-specific authorization.
Administer if the patient signs a pharmacy consent form.
Consent alone does not supply prescriber direction.
Do not administer until the required patient-specific prescription/prescriber direction is in place.
The administration pathway remains prescriber-directed.
Convert the stock dose into an OTC medication.
Administration guidance does not change prescription status.
Ask a technician to select the dose and administer it independently.
That does not satisfy the pharmacist/intern pathway.
steps: Recognize an eligible product
Check patient-specific prescriber authorization before administration
core: Listing of a medication does not eliminate the patient-specific prescription and prescriber-directed nature of administration.
facts: Eligible products are prescribed in single doses and available in single-dose packaging.
trap: Equating product eligibility with standing authority to inject stock.
distinct: Administration-authorization fork rather than product-list recognition.
anti_guess: Each choice preserves the same eligible drug but changes authorization.

stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist administers an eligible patient-specific long-acting antipsychotic under the current MH/SUD pathway. Which workflow principles are consistent with the guidance? Select all that apply.
choices: Use a prescribed single dose supplied in eligible single-dose packaging
The guidance limits eligible products to prescribed single doses/single-dose packaging.
Document the administration in the pharmacy's patient record
Administration requires accountable patient documentation.
Communicate the administration information back to the prescriber as required by the pathway
Prescriber communication supports ongoing assessment.
Allow a cashier to perform the injection after the pharmacist verifies the prescription
The administration authority is not delegated to unlicensed staff.
Skip privacy protections because the medication treats mental illness
Privacy duties remain applicable.
steps: Confirm eligible MH/SUD administration
Apply dose, record, communication, and privacy workflow
core: Eligible MH/SUD administration remains patient-specific, documented, prescriber-connected, and subject to ordinary privacy obligations.
facts: Prescribers must reassess therapy at clinically appropriate intervals.
trap: Treating pharmacy administration as a detached walk-in injection service.
distinct: Post-eligibility workflow is different from Q0146 authorization.
anti_guess: All options sound operationally plausible in an immunization-style workflow.

stem: A Massachusetts long-term-care facility is building its controlled-substance emergency-kit formulary with its single pharmacy provider. The facility wants to include a controlled analgesic. Which framework applies?
choices: Any quantity is allowed if the drug is Schedule VI.
The described item is a controlled analgesic in the CII-V framework.
The facility selects from approved Schedule II-V analgesic choices within the bed-capacity unit limit.
That is the emergency-kit framework.
Only Schedule II analgesics may be included.
The approved category spans CII-V.
Controlled analgesics are prohibited from LTC emergency kits.
They are expressly contemplated.
The pharmacy may ignore facility policies once DPH approves the drug class.
Facility procedures and accountability remain required.
steps: Identify an LTC emergency-kit analgesic
Apply the approved CII-V category and bed-capacity framework
core: LTC facilities may select approved Schedule II-V analgesics within category limits tied to licensed bed capacity.
facts: A separate sedative/anticonvulsant category has its own cap.
trap: Treating a permitted category as either unlimited or Schedule-II-only.
distinct: New special-setting stock authority.
anti_guess: Each distractor represents a believable misreading of schedule versus category limits.

stem: A Massachusetts LTC facility has 120 licensed beds. It wants its emergency kit to contain the maximum allowed number of Schedule II-V analgesic units. What is the current maximum for that analgesic category?
choices: 45 units
That cap applies to the smallest bed tier.
60 units
That cap applies to the next lower tier.
75 units
101-150 beds permits 75 analgesic units.
90 units
That cap applies above 150 beds.
120 units
The cap is not one unit per bed.
steps: Place 120 beds in the 101-150 tier
Apply the analgesic maximum for that tier
core: For 101-150 licensed beds, the LTC emergency-kit analgesic cap is 75 units.
facts: The corresponding sedative/anticonvulsant cap is lower.
trap: Using bed count itself or a neighboring capacity tier.
distinct: No current bank item applies LTC emergency-kit capacity limits.
anti_guess: Four distractors are official neighboring or intuitive values.

stem: Which statements correctly describe Massachusetts LTC emergency-kit safeguards? Select all that apply.
choices: Each Schedule II-V unit should be tamper-evident/resistant and individually packaged as a single dose
The circular specifies that package form.
A facility may use an ADD instead of the traditional locked box when relevant requirements are met
DPH permits ADD substitution.
Schedule VI emergency doses remain subject to procurement, storage, dispensing, administration, recording, and disposal controls
Schedule VI does not escape accountability.
Schedule VI emergency stock is exempt from the facility quality-assurance process
Schedule VI use is monitored by the QA/assessment committee.
Once a kit is approved, controlled-substance accountability policies are optional
Security and accountability policies remain required.
steps: Separate packaging, device, and Schedule VI obligations
Evaluate each safeguard independently
core: LTC emergency kits combine package integrity, accountability, Schedule VI controls, and an optional compliant ADD format.
facts: Facilities need not stock every allowed item or the maximum quantity.
trap: Assuming emergency access relaxes controlled-substance safeguards.
distinct: New kit-safeguard pathway rather than generic pharmacy security.
anti_guess: Three correct statements cover separate operational dimensions.
